summary: Frontend-only visual verification of the enlarged mascot (lion) in the Home '/' EJE CAFETERO section. Scroll worked fine for me (no scroll bug reproduced). Measured absolute page geometry at 1920x1080 and 390x844. RESULT: the lion's bottom now touches the red footer exactly (gap = 0.07px), so the 'no white gap before the red strip' part of the request is satisfied. HOWEVER the image itself did NOT get bigger: it renders at 394.67 x 394.67 px inside a 760px-tall box, so there is ~365px of empty white space ABOVE the lion inside mascot-box. Root cause: Tailwind preflight sets img{max-width:100%} and the lion is a square 1667x1667 webp inside a 394.67px-wide grid column, so 'h-full' is overridden by the width cap and aspect ratio. Since the previous CSS had scale-110 on the same 394px render, the lion is effectively ~10% SMALLER than before, not 'notablemente más grande'. Regression check passed: FESTIVAL and PREMIER columns render correctly side by side, no overlap/clipped text (extra white space below them as expected). Mobile view unchanged and correct (lion 342x342, 80px gap to footer).

rca_of_the_issue: Tailwind's preflight applies max-width:100% to img. The mascot is in the middle column of a 3-column max-w-7xl grid (~394.67px wide). With a 1:1 aspect asset, the width cap forces the rendered height to 394.67px, so the 'h-full' (100% of the 760px box) never takes effect; the flex items-end alignment then pushes the small image to the bottom, which is why the bottom edge correctly meets the footer while a large white gap remains above.
